dashboard.description: Explore DNS queries to Edge DNS and Global Traffic Manager.

options.content:
Akamai / Hydrolix Internal - Please read:


This eDNS / GTM dashboard has new summary table dependencies and requires additional configuration after importing it manually to a customer's Grafana organization in order to work correctly.

If you would like to provide a customer with this particular dashboard or an entire set of TrafficPeak Certified Reference dashboards, we highly recommend reaching out to Hydrolix support via akamai-ps@hydrolix.io to ensure all dependencies are met and the dashboards are configured as needed.

In case you really need to manually import this dashboard to a customer's Grafana organisation and you are sure all dependencies are already in place, please find the instructions below. Please read and follow the instructions carefully.

Click to expand instructions

Steps to export the dashboard

  • Click on the "Export" button in the top right section of the dashboard, then click on "Export as JSON"
  • In the sidebar that opened, enable the toggle to "Export the dashboard to use in another instance"
  • Click on "Download file" to download a copy of the JSON file to your computer

Steps to import the dashboard

  • Go to the customer's Grafana organisation and navigate to the "TrafficPeak Certified Reference Dashboards" / "DNS" folder
  • Click on the "New" button, then click "Import"
  • Click on the "Upload dashboard JSON file" banner and select the dashboard JSON file you downloaded in the steps described above
  • In the "Import dashboard" page, it is necessary to adjust some variables depending on the customer type (dedicated or shared):
    • Do not change the name, folder or UID of the dashboard
    • Select the "hydrolix-hydrolix-datasource" available (there should only be one available option per customer)
    • edns_summary_hour / edns variable configuration:
      • For dedicated customers, leave all values as-is
      • For shared customers, please replace the values for the variables mentioned below with the following values (replacing example customer_x with the correct shared customer name):

        Variable Value
        edns_summary_hour customer_x.edns_summary_hour
        edns customer_x.edns

  • Double check all inputs are in-line with the steps above, then click on "Import"


Additional configuration

Due to a Grafana bug, there is an additional configuration step needed to make the new adhoc-filter work as expected:

  • Click on "Edit" in the top right section of the dashboard, then click on "Settings"
  • Click on the "Variables" tab, then click on the "filter" variable
  • Under the "Ad-hoc options", click on the "Data Source" dropdown menu and select the available Hydrolix data source
  • Now click on "Save dashboard" in the top right section, then click on the "Save" button in the right side menu bar that opened up
  • Re-open the dashboard and confirm the adhoc-filter is working as expected:
    • Click on the "Filter by label values" text box of the adhoc-filter in the top left section of the dashboard
    • Verify that a list of columns appears
    • If you see "An error has occurred fetching labels. Click to retry", please ensure you have performed the steps outlined above
  • If you keep seeing the adhoc-filter error or any other unexpected behavior like panels not able to query the data, please reach out to the Hydrolix support (akamai-support@hydrolix.io), ideally including a screenshot and the error messages you are seeing.

Banner Removal

Once the dashboard has been confirmed to be working as expected (including the adhoc-filter), it is essential to remove this informational banner:

  • Click on "Edit" in the top right section of the dashboard
  • Click on the three-dot menu on the top right corner of this text panel
  • Click on "Remove"
  • Now click on "Save dashboard" in the top right section, then click on the "Save" button in the ride side menu bar that opened up

panels.description: Total number of requests in the selected time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 
${cnt_all} as count
FROM ${table}
WHERE $__timeFilter(${timestamp})
    AND $__adHocFilter() 
SETTINGS hdx_query_max_execution_time=60, hdx_query_admin_comment='db=${__dashboard}; dp=Total Requests; du=${__user.login}'

panels.title: Total Requests

targets.rawSql:
with (
  select topK(20)(requestName) 
  FROM ${table}
  WHERE $__timeFilter(${timestamp})
      AND $__adHocFilter() 
) as top_items

SELECT 
requestName,
${cnt_all} as count,
$__timeInterval(timeStamp) as time
FROM ${table}
  WHERE $__timeFilter(${timestamp})
      AND $__adHocFilter() 
      AND has(top_items, requestName)
group by time,requestName
order by time asc
SETTINGS hdx_query_max_execution_time=60, hdx_query_admin_comment='db=${__dashboard}; dp=Requests Over Time per; du=${__user.login}'

panels.title: Distinct Ports

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 
country, 
${cnt_all} as count
FROM ${table}
WHERE $__timeFilter(${timestamp})
  AND $__adHocFilter() 
group by country
order by count desc
LIMIT 1000
SETTINGS hdx_query_max_execution_time=60, hdx_query_admin_comment='db=${__dashboard}; dp=Requests per Country; du=${__user.login}'

WITH country_totals AS (
    SELECT
        country,
        ${cnt_all} AS total_count
    FROM ${table}
    WHERE $__timeFilter(${timestamp})
        AND $__adHocFilter() 
GROUP BY country
),

country_hostname_counts AS (
    SELECT
        country,
        answer as hostname,
        ${cnt_all} AS hostname_count
    FROM ${table}
    WHERE $__timeFilter(${timestamp})
        AND $__adHocFilter() 
GROUP BY country, hostname
)
    SELECT
        chc.country,
        chc.hostname,
        chc.hostname_count,
        ct.total_count,
        (chc.hostname_count / ct.total_count) * 100 AS hostname_percentage
    FROM country_hostname_counts chc
    JOIN country_totals ct ON chc.country = ct.country

SETTINGS hdx_query_max_execution_time=60, hdx_query_admin_comment='db=${__dashboard}; dp=Hostname distribution by Country; du=${__user.login}'

SELECT 
state, 
${cnt_all} as count
FROM ${table}
WHERE $__timeFilter(${timestamp})
    AND $__adHocFilter() 
group by state
order by count desc
LIMIT 200
SETTINGS hdx_query_max_execution_time=60, hdx_query_admin_comment='db=${__dashboard}; dp=Requests per Region; du=${__user.login}'

WITH state_totals AS (
    SELECT
        state,
        ${cnt_all} AS total_count
    FROM ${table}
    WHERE $__timeFilter(${timestamp})
        AND $__adHocFilter() 
    GROUP BY state
),

state_hostname_counts AS (
    SELECT
        state,
        answer as hostname,
        ${cnt_all} AS hostname_count
    FROM ${table}
    WHERE $__timeFilter(${timestamp})
        AND $__adHocFilter() 
    GROUP BY state, hostname
)
    SELECT
        chc.state,
        chc.hostname,
        chc.hostname_count,
        ct.total_count,
        (chc.hostname_count / ct.total_count) * 100 AS hostname_percentage
    FROM state_hostname_counts chc
    JOIN state_totals ct ON chc.state = ct.state
SETTINGS hdx_query_max_execution_time=60, hdx_query_admin_comment='db=${__dashboard}; dp=Hostname distribution by Region; du=${__user.login}'

options.content:
Link to Akamai TechDocs Field Definitions here

Data element Examples Description
Epoch timestamp 1710167865 The Unix epoch timestamp of the log entry and its transaction.
Date 07/12/2020 The UTC date for log entry and its transaction.
Resolver IP 2600:141b:b000::1736:a142 The IP address of the DNS resolver making the request.
Request port 37041 The port number of the DNS resolver making the request.
Request name nxdomain.edgedns.zone The query name of the request.
Class IN The DNS class of the request.
A : Internet
CH : Chaos
HS : Hesiod
Any : Any other
(Note: almost exclusively it's A>
Request type A : Request Record
AAAA : IPv6 Request Record
CNAME : Canonical Name which redirects to another name
MX : Mail Exchange
TXT : Text record
NS : Indicates which DNS server is authoritative for the domain
SRV : Service Record. Specifies ports for service
PTR : Pointer - maps IP address to domain name for reverse lookups
SOA : Start of Authority - provides information about the domain and primary DNS server		 The request's DNS record type.
EDNS0 flag ## E The EDNS0 Client Subnet (ECS) indicator, either E or blank. This is used to provide more accurate routing information by augmenting information about the resolver IP with information about the client subnet Akamai can make more informed resolution decisions.
EDNS0 size 1220 The ECS (Edge DNS Client Subnet) field size in bytes.
DNSSEC flag ## D The DNSSEC indicator, either D or blank.
TCP flag ## T The TCP indicator, either T or blank.
Answers 3:NXDOMAIN The request answers for a request query name.
Time 14:37:45 GMT The UTC time for log entry and its transaction.


Other Links

  • Article in ECS (Edge DNS Client Subnet) here
  • RFC Standard on ECS here
